# `Q-9-14` — Duplicate Macro Definition

> Two `<cs:macro>` elements share the same `name` attribute.

## What this means

Macro names form a namespace: each `<cs:macro name="...">` must
be unique within a style. This error fires when the parser
finds a second `<cs:macro>` with a name it has already seen.
The message identifies the second definition (the first one is
treated as authoritative).

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **A copy-paste during editing** that duplicated a macro and
  did not rename it.
- **A merge conflict resolution** that kept both versions of a
  macro instead of picking one.
- **A migration from a different citation framework** that
  combined two source macros into one CSL macro file without
  renaming.

## How to fix

Decide which definition you want to keep, and either delete the
other or rename it. If both definitions are meaningfully
different but you cannot tell which is correct, the original
upstream style (CSL repository, journal-provided style) is the
source of truth.
